implementation: Native write/truncate preflight the prospective mutation against its exact Working snapshot before changing private bytes. Read-only canonical traversal verifies only necessary existing pages and old byte gaps; it creates no new content hashes, CAS objects or FULL checkpoint. Full-covered old chunks and zero ranges need no old data. Existing dirty paths are included after recovery/headless writes/partial failures.

Missing native data/page preflight returns, releasing cursor, bounded scratch, three background buffer permits and journal guards before authenticated BaseWait. File.state is not held. Same exact operation/working snapshot is revalidated after arrival and again under File.state before mutation. Adapter capacity precedes the same-file gate. Context and adapter fence cancellation are checked during preflight and between bounded write pieces; stale preflight never replaces concurrent bytes.

CheckpointEdit and canonical prepare use local reads exclusively; prepare never calls BaseWait. Fsync obtains a FULL checkpoint before local preparation/publication. Losing an acknowledged write base produces immediate CONTENT_UNAVAILABLE, zero demand-hook calls and retained Saved/private bytes; local restoration allows retry. No waiting for peer/replication acknowledgement.

Headless mutation remains supported with a needs_preflight marker; recovered Saved sessions start marked. Complete native writes/resizes clear the marker only after success; partial failures retain it. Native length mirrors session length on error. No durable format, user_version4, provider API, wire/event encoding or production activation change.

One new legacy unit proves fully private replacement can resize/prepare with the original whole-file object absent and tests local cancellation. One 1GiB deduplicated-tree/4KiB edit parent bounds preflight existing reads/pages and excludes fixture seeding. Three new transport parents cover missing-local-base fsync, concurrent stale preflight and shrink/grow zeroes. Prior hydration cases now require pre-write base preparation and peer disconnect before fsync, including a real WinFsp/FUSE write/sync/reopen parent.
development: An early missing-local-base parent used an unsupported hello peer probe after its fsync assertions; changed to the existing authenticated capabilities probe. A new legacy unit initially failed compilation because checkpoint returns Option<SaveCheckpoint>; correctly unwrapped it. These draft failures and all mutable-source preliminary runs are retained separately and are not final qualification or extra passes. No timing assertion or release gate relaxed.

Prior CCR17 evidence and its two diagnostic source archives remain immutable history. Its fsync-network and partial-data permit gaps are corrected by this stage, not reinterpreted as a weaker replication-acknowledgement contract.
not_qualified: COW structural-demand admission after dispatcher idle/saturation is not measured here. Existing structural idle backoff can reach640ms; original250ms foreground-admission release gate remains open.

Generic-provider mounted COW canonical rebuilding, legacy whole-base remote conversion hydration and missing reused chunks of a newly published root before peers learn its new authorized reference remain open. No bare-hash fallback or authorization bypass.

Native namespace create/delete/rename/atomic replacement/open-handle identity, long-lived writer metadata/time rebasing, autonomous startup/conflict retry and complete production lifecycle/status/poison/accept-error/shutdown remain open.

Automatic close/metadata batching, private-reader independence during journal FULL fsync, complete root/retention/GC/retirement and sustained physical storage progress, aggregate queue/byte/SQL/CPU/disk/RSS fairness/shutdown/30min soak, WP6.5 build/cache/change journal, WP6.6 negotiation/activation/migration/downgrade/old-executable/handoff and all original release gates remain required. No production activation, user mount, migration or live CAS deletion.
